subject: Scaling runway & renewal sync
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sara Potts <sara.potts@aureliahealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Scaling runway & renewal sync

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the time last week. As Aurelia heads into the Q3 rollout, I wanted to get ahead of the renewal conversation and the expansion you referenced (additional inference capacity for image-processing pipelines). High-level proposal we discussed:

- Renewal: 12-month renewal at current committed rate.
- Mid-contract top-up: +30% capacity (monthly true-up) starting July 1 to support pilot traffic.
- Co-term: align the top-up to the existing renewal date (co-term in Oct) with an annualize option at the next renewal point.

Before I draft a formal addendum, quick asks so I configure the pricing worksheet correctly:
1) Do you want the top-up billed pro-rata monthly or as a one-time invoice?
2) Would Aurelia consider a modest multi-month discount for pre-purchasing the top-up to smooth billing? (we can model 5–12% depending on commit length)
3) Is procurement the right owner for contract language, or should I loop legal?

Attaching a sketch of the product addendum and a blank pricing worksheet. I can swing back with two concrete options (monthly true-up vs pre-pay credit) for you and procurement to pick from.

Attachments: Aurelia_MA_plan_v3.pdf (sketch), redwood-pricing-worksheet-AH.xlsx (model)

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | (415) 555-0181
From: Sara Potts <sara.potts@aureliahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurelia Health Procurement <procurement@aureliahealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T10:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Scaling runway & renewal sync

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few quick answers:
- We prefer monthly true-up for flexibility during the pilot.
- Procurement will need pricing scenarios; they prefer to avoid large up-front spends but are open to a small discount if it lowers unit cost.
- Please loop in legal only if there are new T&Cs; procurement will handle redlines for SOW/addenda first.

A few constraints from our side: any new committed capacity must include an option for a short notice scale-down after 90 days (we need elasticity for pilot season). Also, can you confirm that data residency for the pilot remains in us-west region?

Cc'ing procurement to keep them in the loop.

—Sara
Sara Potts
VP Product Operations | Aurelia Health
sara.potts@aureliahealth.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Potts <sara.potts@aureliahealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-07T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Scaling runway & renewal sync — pricing options for review

Kimberly / Tessa —

Looping you both for a quick internal alignment. Aurelia is asking for: monthly true-up top-up (+~30%), optional pre-pay discount if they want to smooth unit cost, and a 90-day short-notice scale-down for the pilot window. They also require region lock to us-west for pilot data residency.

My recommended paths to present (two options):
A) Monthly true-up (preferred by customer):
  - +30% capacity added July 1; billed month-over-month at committed rate; 90-day scale-down allowed up to 20% of the top-up without penalty; no pre-pay discount.
B) Pre-pay credit (discounted):
  - Customer prepays an amount equal to 3 months of the top-up at 8% discount to unit rate; credits applied monthly; scale-down allowed but credits are non-refundable — we offer a one-time reallocation to other Redwood products within 6 months.

Questions for you:
- Kimberly: any legal concerns with the 90-day short-notice scale-down and reallocation clause?
- Tessa: can finance handle the pre-pay credit flow (one invoice, spread over 3 months) and how would revenue recognition prefer we record?

I've attached the pricing worksheet (filled with rough numbers) and a proposed addendum template (SOW addendum). If we can sign off on one option this week, I can send to procurement with numbers and a DocuSign link.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-worksheet-AH.xlsx, AH_SOW_addendum.docx

Thanks —
Jordan
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Scaling runway & renewal sync — pricing options for review

Jordan / Tessa —

Reviewed. Legal is comfortable with option A (monthly true-up) if we codify the scale-down cap and define the operational triggers. A few redline notes on the addendum:
- Define "scale-down" window (90 days) and cap (max 20% of top-up) — beyond cap requires 30-day notice and potential reconciliation invoice.
- We should include a short runbook for data residency (us-west) and a rollback plan if region capacity is unavailable — protects both sides.
- For option B (pre-pay), recommend we include a clause allowing limited credit transfer to other Redwood services to avoid refund obligations.

If we present both, procurement can pick. For speed, create an addendum with option A default and option B as an alternate checkbox (customer initials required). I can turn around a redline and upload to DocuSign later today.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

Subject: Updated addendum + DocuSign (two options)

Sara —

Thanks for the confirm — attached is the update per Kimberly's redlines. Summary of the package I've uploaded to DocuSign:

Option A (default) — Monthly true-up- Top-up: +30% (start July 1) billed monthly at current committed unit rate- 90-day scale-down window allowing up to 20% reduction without penalty; beyond that, 30 days notice + reconciliation- Data residency: pilot workloads pinned to us-west region

Option B (alternate) — 3-month pre-pay credit (optional)- One invoice up front for 3 months of top-up at 8% discount; credits applied monthly; credits non-refundable but transferable to other Redwood products within 6 months

Link: https://www.docusign.com/instance/sign/abc123-aurelia

Attachments: redwood-pricing-worksheet-AH.xlsx (numbers filled), AH_SOW_addendum.docx (redline incorporated), Aurelia_MA_plan_v3.pdf (context)

Next steps: pick A or B, procurement signs via DocuSign, we schedule kickoff for July 1. If procurement prefers an annualize/co-term later instead of immediate top-up, we can model that in the worksheet before signing.

Looking forward —
